intro.title: useDebounce
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useDebounce` that delays the update of a value until a specified time has passed without further changes. You will learn the core concept of debouncing, which is a technique to limit how often a function runs, improving performance by preventing excessive updates or API calls. The main technologies involved are React hooks (specifically `useState` and `useEffect`) and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll create a reusable hook that can be applied to scenarios like search inputs, where you want to wait for the user to stop typing before triggering an action.
intro.usecase: The useDebounce hook is essential for optimizing performance in interactive UIs where frequent user input triggers expensive operations. In search interfaces like GitHub's repository search or Google's autocomplete, debouncing prevents excessive API calls with every keystroke. Dashboard filter panels with real-time data updates use debouncing to avoid overwhelming servers with rapid filter changes. Form validation for fields like email or username availability checks also benefits from debouncing to reduce unnecessary validation requests while users are still typing.
